50 Boutique Wine Importers and Distributors in the USA
29/10/2026 From specialists in natural wines and family estates to regional wholesalers serving independent retailers, these are companies wineries should know when building their U.S. distribution strategy.
For a boutique winery, the right U.S. partner does more than arrange the movement of bottles. It understands the producer, identifies suitable accounts, and gives its sales team a clear reason to recommend the wine.
That makes portfolio fit essential. A specialist in Italian family estates may be well suited to an unfamiliar indigenous variety. A natural-wine importer may place particular importance on farming and cellar practices. A regional distributor may offer the focused market coverage a small winery can realistically support.
The following guide brings together 50 boutique and specialist wine importers and distributors serving the United States. Some are small businesses with tightly focused portfolios; others are larger companies that maintain a strong commitment to independent producers.
Official websites and company portfolio information were checked for this article on October 28, 2026. This is an editorial guide, not a sales ranking. Importing and wholesale distribution are different services, and inclusion does not mean a company is currently accepting new producers.
Importers With a Strong Grower and Estate Focus
1. Kermit Lynch Wine Merchant
Kermit Lynch Wine Merchant imports wines from France and Italy, with a portfolio spanning celebrated regions and less familiar appellations. Its producer-centered approach makes it an important reference for wineries studying specialist importing. Producers should examine the existing growers and regional coverage before proposing a fit.
2. Rosenthal Wine Merchant
Rosenthal Wine Merchant emphasizes small, family-owned estates and wines that communicate their origins. Its portfolio includes producers from France, Italy, Switzerland, Spain, and Austria. For wineries, the central question is whether their vineyards, winemaking, and regional identity complement the merchant’s established approach.
3. Louis/Dressner Selections
Louis/Dressner Selections has longstanding relationships with independent growers and a strong interest in farming and winemaking practices. Its website provides extensive producer information and harvest reports. Wineries researching the business should be ready to discuss their work in the vineyard and cellar in detail.
4. Skurnik Wines & Spirits
Skurnik Wines & Spirits combines national importing with direct wholesale distribution in selected states. Its portfolio includes boutique producers from around the world. Suppliers should distinguish between a national import relationship and a proposal for a specific wholesale market, then approach the relevant team accordingly.
5. T. Edward Wines & Spirits
T. Edward Wines & Spirits began with boutique estates and continues to emphasize family-owned producers, craftsmanship, and authenticity. Its business includes importing and distribution. A winery’s introduction should explain the people behind the wine, its production philosophy, and its commercial role within the portfolio.
6. Bowler Wine
Bowler Wine is a New York-based importer and distributor focused on naturally made, small-production wines. Its selection emphasizes personality, regional character, and family growers. Wineries should research both its direct producer relationships and the other import portfolios it represents before making an introduction. NYC Wine Spirits Importer Distributor
7. European Cellars
European Cellars imports wines from family-owned properties practicing responsible viticulture. Its roots in France and Spain have expanded into other origins. Producers should assess how their wines express place and whether they add a distinct regional or stylistic contribution to the existing selection.
8. De Maison Selections
De Maison Selections is a national importer with a strong commitment to artisanal properties, regional heritage, and producer independence. Its business distinguishes national importing from direct distribution through De Maison East. Wineries should establish which relationship they are seeking before presenting their portfolio.
9. Polaner Selections
Polaner Selections combines established reference-point producers with smaller wineries, indigenous varieties, and less familiar regions. Its selection includes traditional producers and growers using organic or biodynamic practices. A compelling proposal should explain both the wine’s individuality and its value at the intended selling price.
10. Martine’s Wines
Martine’s Wines operates as an importer and wholesaler, with producer profiles and current wine information on its website. Its portfolio includes wines from established French regions and distinctive estates such as Domaine des Ardoisières. Suppliers should study the relevant regional selection before proposing additional representation. Importer & Wholesaler since 1979
Natural Wine and Small-Production Specialists
11. Jenny & François Selections
Jenny & François Selections focuses on natural wines from small growers. Its philosophy considers both vineyard practices and cellar methods. Producers researching the company should prepare a transparent account of farming, fermentation, additions, and production, alongside the practical information needed to evaluate a U.S. launch.
12. Zev Rovine Selections
Zev Rovine Selections works with growers who farm organically or biodynamically and favor minimal intervention in the cellar. Its producer list spans numerous countries. Wineries should assess philosophical fit and regional overlap, rather than assume a natural-wine identity alone creates an opening in the portfolio.
13. Selection Massale
Selection Massale imports natural wines from small wineries, emphasizing precision and drinkability. Its stated approach favors naturally fermented wines and growers working largely organically or biodynamically. Producers should explain how their practices translate into the wine’s character and consistency.
14. José Pastor Selections
José Pastor Selections champions small growers and traditionally made wines, with deep Spanish roots and a portfolio extending to other origins. Its selection includes regional grapes and distinctive vineyard environments. Wineries should explain what makes their wines an authentic expression of their particular place.
15. SelectioNaturel
SelectioNaturel specializes in Italian wines made in small quantities using natural and traditional methods. Its narrow focus makes regional and philosophical alignment especially important. Italian producers should study the represented growers and explain what their wines contribute beyond an appealing production story.
16. Vom Boden
Vom Boden focuses on small estates and growers whose work or locations sit outside the obvious mainstream. Its website includes current material on German wine. Producers considering the company should research its selection carefully and explain the vineyard, regional, and stylistic reasons their wines belong in that conversation.
17. Schatzi Wines
Schatzi Wines emphasizes the connection between growers and wine drinkers, with authenticity, sustainability, and terroir central to its approach. Its portfolio is built around producer relationships. Wineries should prepare clear information about their farming, wines, and expectations for a long-term importing partnership.
18. Olmstead Wine Co.
Olmstead Wine Co. is a Massachusetts distributor explicitly focused on natural wine. It provides a regional prospect for producers and importers whose wines fit that category. Suppliers should examine the portfolio and establish the current route for introducing new wines to the team.
19. Walden Selections
Walden Selections is a Washington State importer and distributor of wine and other beverages. It also appears in SelectioNaturel’s distribution network. Producers researching Washington should review the existing selection and discuss the specific importing or wholesale services required.
20. Nomadic Distribution
Nomadic Distribution presents itself as an importer and distributor of organic and natural wines. Its website includes producer information and a natural-wine shop. Suppliers should begin by reviewing the current producer list and confirming the relevant markets, portfolio needs, and submission process.
Regional and Country Specialists
21. The Piedmont Guy
The Piedmont Guy is a U.S.-based importer specializing in family-owned wineries from Piedmont. Its focused portfolio makes it particularly relevant to producers from that region. A pitch should explain the winery’s local identity, varieties, and position alongside the estates already represented.
22. Oliver McCrum Wines & Spirits
Oliver McCrum Wines & Spirits imports small-production Italian wines and operates distribution activities. Its stated preferences include clarity, freshness, indigenous varieties, and transparent winemaking. Producers should connect those characteristics with pricing and an account proposition that a sales team can readily explain.
23. Dalla Terra Italian Wine & Spirits
Dalla Terra describes its business as a national agent and direct importer for a select group of artisan, family-owned Italian wineries and spirits producers. Italian suppliers should understand its direct-import model and assess the existing regional portfolio before approaching the company.
24. Indigenous Selections
Indigenous Selections represents a curated group of Italian wineries selected for authenticity and regional character. Its portfolio covers origins including Piedmont, Tuscany, Veneto, Campania, Sicily, and Friuli. Producers should show how their wines offer a distinctive expression within the relevant region and price segment.
25. Porto Vino
Porto Vino maintains a French and Italian portfolio that includes producers from regions such as the Loire, Burgundy, Piedmont, and Sicily. Its website provides a detailed producer list. Suppliers should examine that regional coverage and explain where their wines add a meaningful point of difference.
26. North Berkeley Imports
North Berkeley Imports sources wines from France and Italy, combining importing with selected direct-market portfolios and distribution partners. Its offer reaches restaurants, wine shops, and collectors. Producers should distinguish the national portfolio opportunity from the company’s specific wholesale-market activities.
27. Michael Corso Selections
Michael Corso Selections is a specialist importer with a strong French wine focus. Its portfolio includes regions such as Alsace, Burgundy, the Loire, and the Rhône. Producers should present their regional credentials alongside a clear explanation of value and likely U.S. positioning.
28. Charles Neal Selections
Charles Neal Selections is a San Francisco-based importer and distributor with French wines and a substantial spirits selection. Its specialist approach makes it relevant to producers with a clear regional identity. Suppliers should explain the wine’s quality and commercial relevance without relying on small production as the sole selling point.
29. Brazos Wine Imports
Brazos Wine Imports focuses on artisan wines from Argentina, Chile, and Uruguay. Its stated interests include estate-grown, small-production wines that express specific places. South American producers should prepare detailed vineyard information and explain how the wines differ from more familiar market offerings.
30. Little Peacock Imports
Little Peacock Imports emphasizes a curated selection of family wineries, with producer listings covering Australia, France, Italy, and New Zealand. Its positioning combines discovery with commercial performance. Suppliers should explain why the wine is distinctive and how it can earn repeat purchases.
Curated Importers With Broader Portfolios
31. Grand Cru Selections
Grand Cru Selections is a New York-based importer and distributor with a strong fine-wine portfolio. Its producer information covers Champagne, Burgundy, and other regions. Wineries should research the existing estates closely and present a precise case for stylistic, regional, and commercial fit.
32. Coeur Wine Co.
Coeur Wine Co. emphasizes long-term producer relationships and wines it considers honest and authentic. Its website provides producer information and distribution partners. Suppliers should focus their introduction on the wine’s quality, its intended customer, and the practical foundations of a lasting relationship.
33. Communal Brands
Communal Brands combines production, importing, and distribution, with an emphasis on environmentally conscious wines and contemporary presentation. Its offer includes alternative formats such as boxed wine. Wineries should consider how product format, quality, and customer occasion work together within this business model.
34. Vine Connections
Vine Connections imports and distributes wines from family producers in origins including Argentina, Chile, Italy, France, and California. Its website provides trade tools such as technical sheets and shelf talkers. Producers should prepare a similarly complete set of materials when seeking representation. Global Wine, Sake & Spirits Importer
35. Massanois
Massanois is a national importer with direct distribution in selected markets. Its portfolio emphasizes quality-driven, family-owned wineries and distilleries. Suppliers should determine whether they need importing, direct wholesale distribution, or both, then tailor the proposal to the appropriate operation.
36. Banville Wine Merchants
Banville Wine Merchants combines national importing with wholesale operations in selected U.S. markets. Its approach centers on a selective, quality-focused portfolio. Producers should distinguish the national import opportunity from local distribution and identify the specific customer and price tier their wines would serve.
37. Regal Wine Imports
Regal Wine Imports maintains importing and distribution activities across wine and other beverage categories. Its website includes producer portfolios, trade information, and recent company content. Wineries should examine the relevant portfolio and market operation before proposing a new regional or stylistic addition.
38. Artisans & Vines
Artisans & Vines sources wines from Europe and several New World origins, emphasizing terroir and value. Its business includes importing, marketing, and distribution relationships. Suppliers should clarify the proposed territory and responsibilities, then connect their wine’s identity with a realistic market-development plan.
39. Wine Traditions

Hello, my name is Camille.
I was raised in Paris and the Loire Valley amongst the vineyards and caves. By the age of 16 I was skipping school to go to wine tastings. My mother noticed my enthusiasm for drinking so she enrolled me in my first wine classes. My initial epicurean interests soon became a career choice, and in 2003 I graduated from the Ecole Hoteliere de Paris, then completed a Bachelors degree in hotel & restaurant management at Universite Dauphine. Internships as a chef de partie in northern England and as assistant food & beverage manager in a four-star hotel in Paris, strengthened my bacchanalian desire to work in this field; more specifically in the wine industry.
My first official wine internship was at Morrell Wine & Company. After two years on the retail side, I wanted to get a sense of the import and distribution world so I started working for Frederick Wildman and Son’s. I worked like a mad woman for 5 years selling wine and traveling the world to taste and meet winemakers. During the summer of 2011, while traveling through the vineyards of France, meeting winemakers, I came to the realization that I was drawn to wines that were more on the “natural” side; and Camille Rivière Selections was born. Presently, I live in Paris with my wife and daughter.

results.rawContent:
About Michael Corso Selections
Our goal at Michael Corso Selections is simple: to import top quality French wines and spirits at the best possible prices. Our belief is in the growers: good growers will always make good wine. We travel regularly and extensively in France seeking those producers whose wines offer a classic profile and express the unique qualities of their specific terroirs. We work predominantly with small vignerons who are keenly aware of the importance of the land that they pass on to their children and grandchildren. Hence, many of the wines we import are produced sustainably, many organically and all are made with a respect for quality. We believe in letting the winemakers make the wine; we are not interventionist importers. We like wines that are meant to be enjoyed with food, wines with freshness and acidity, wines that are finely balanced and not overpowering. Since 1972, Mike Corso has worked in virtually all aspects of wine sales: retail, restaurant, wholesale distribution, importer representative and importer, always with a concentration on European wines. Michael Corso Selections offers the expertise of over 50 years of experience in the wine trade, the quality of hand-selected wines from small, family domaines and the character of wines rooted in traditional styles.
Our Team

Michael Corso
Founder and Managing Partner
Mike Corso brings a wealth of experience to the company. Starting in 1972 at The House of Glunz, Chicago’s oldest wine retail shop, he has worked in all aspects of wine sales at the restaurant, wholesale distributor and importer levels. After a 7-year association with World Shippers & Importers of Philadelphia, where he succeeded Robert Kacher as National Sales Manager, he spent 16 years as Import Manager at Union Beverage in Chicago and helped create Chicago Wine Merchants, one of the leading fine wine distributers in the U.S. The basis of the Michael Corso Selections portfolio was created during this time. In 2008 he established MCS as an independent importer of high quality estate wines and spirits from France and Italy. The portfolio is his creation and is an extension of his taste in wine, which is very traditional, and of his long experience in the wine trade. Mike’s interests include Art History, French and Italian language, fine food and ice hockey. He has a B.A. from Boston College and spent two years of study in Italy at the Loyola University Rome Center and at the Universita Per Stranieri in Perugia, Italy.

Elizabeth Corso
Managing Partner
Beth Corso studied theatre at West Virginia University and The Goodman School of Drama, which inevitably led to a career in the hospitality industry.  During a diverse 20-year run in fine dining restaurants, Beth had a constant involvement in wine and restaurant wine programs. She later moved fully to the wine side as Chicago Metro Manager for Wilson Daniels, where she enjoyed a highly successful career representing such icons as Romanée-Conti, Maison Faiveley, Domaine Leflaive, and Salon Champagne, along with the outstanding American wines in this famous portfolio. Today she oversees all internal operations of Michael Corso Selections, and travels extensively each year to the wine regions of France and Italy.  She is a passionate cook and her dinner parties are the stuff of legend. She is also a voracious reader, and classical music provides the soundtrack to her life.

Matthew Corso
Operations Manager
Matthew grew up around wine and is excited to be part of the family company. He relocated from Washington, DC, his longtime home, to Chicago. He will be working on all aspects of internal administration and brings a wealth of professional experience to the company. Matthew has over 15 years’ experience in communications, events and program management, and is adept at managing customer service requests and working in a deadline driven environment. Prior to joining the company, he worked in international development at the U.S. Agency for International Development, as a consultant for DAI, and at the U.S. Global Leadership Coalition and Sister Cities International. Matthew is an avid internationalist, wine enthusiast, and enjoys traveling, cooking, reading, bocce, darts, running, and volunteering in his local community. He has a M.A. in International Affairs from the Elliott School at The George Washington University and a B.S. in Political Science and German from the University of Wisconsin-Eau Claire in Eau Claire, WI.

Donn Danielson
Director of Sales
Donn Danielson brings a passion for wine, especially French wine, with over 30 years of experience in the industry working with distributors, wine suppliers, and National Accounts On and Off Premise. Donn grew up in Chicago working in restaurants with his family and as a means of supporting himself in college. He got started in the wine business with his first job out of college running the wine department for Marshall Field’s in Chicago. In the evenings, he attended Chicago Wine School to become more proficient in wine and wine education. In 1994, Donn joined Chicago Wine Merchants, a division of Union Beverage Company, where he first met and worked with Mike. After several years and different roles including Sales Representative, District Manager and finally Brand Manager, Donn decided to move to Northern California in 1999 to begin his career as a supplier. He worked for The Hess Collection Winery, Grgich Hills Estate, and Folio Fine Wine Partners/Michael Mondavi. In 2015, Donn and his wife Catherine and daughter Ava moved to New Orleans where he joined European Cellars/Eric Solomon Selections as Director of National Accounts On and Off Premise. Most recently Donn was the Vice President of Sales – National Accounts, On Premise at The Mark Wine Group. When not working Donn loves to cook, play golf, and spend time with his family. He has a Business degree from Indiana University and is a huge fan of all the Chicago sports teams, with a real affinity for the Chicago Blackhawks!

Dave Sink
Illinois Market Manager
Dave Sink is an Illinois native. Born and raised just south of Chicago, he attended the University of Illinois to study Aviation and History and then returned to Chicago after college to pursue a career in food, wine, and hospitality and to start a family a few years after. Working all aspects in the front of house at several chef-driven restaurants in the 1990s led to a love and understanding of haute cuisine, which then uncovered a now lifelong fascination into fine wines. The 2000s opened a new door into the distribution realm when Dave joined the opening team for Maverick Wine IL. For 20+ years in the Chicago market, he helped Maverick build beverage programs, grew lifelong relationships, traveled to several wine regions, all while meeting numerous mentors and icons in the field. Dave is a long-suffering Bears and White Sox fan, an avid cyclist and OG gamer. Other interests include movies, music, travel, and a Negroni or two.

Steve Vesely
Midwest Sales Representative
Steve brings over 28 years in beverage sales experience to the team. He met Mike during his tenure with Chicago Wine Merchants in 2003, where he represented, among other things, their French Portfolio which would become the basis for Michael Corso Selections.
Steve has traveled throughout the world’s wine regions, and extensively in France. He loves history, music and is a bonafide sports fanatic.

Jodie Hellman
Southwest Regional Manager
Jodie Hellman was born in Philadelphia and then moved to Florida and now resides in Las Vegas. She went to school to study commercial art, but always kept getting drawn back into hospitality. Once she moved to Las Vegas, she got bit by the wine bug. It started with daily training classes at work, then grew when she became part of the opening team at craftsteak at MGM with Tom Collicchio. After a few years, she moved to open Daniel Boulud at Wynn Las Vegas as a sommelier and worked at all the outlets on property. From hospitality, she moved to the sales side starting with a family winery in California and eventually with imports from all over the globe. She recently became an Italian Wine Ambassador as part of a program with VinItaly and the Italian Trade Association. Jodie is a huge Bruce Springsteen fan and enjoys traveling, movies and spending time with family and friends.

Chris Miller
California/ Pacific Northwest Regional Manager
Chris Miller started working at Young’s Market Company in Santa Cruz County in 1998, and by 2001 had worked his way up to the Northern California Market Manager for Wilson Daniels. In 2008, after his tenure with WD and working as a Sales Manager for Chambers and Chambers, he moved to Los Angeles where he worked as a restaurant wine director then later spent close to 4 years as the southern California Italian wine buyer for K&L Wine Merchants in Hollywood. Returning to Northern California in 2013, he held managerial positions at Massanois, Grandes Places Selections and Winebow. In 2022, he brings this wealth of knowledge and experience to Michael Corso Selections. Chris has traveled exhaustively throughout the wine regions of France, Italy, Spain, Germany, Austria, Hungary and North America. He enjoys spending time with his wife and two boys, hiking, camping, kayaking and drinking Champagne, Burgundy, Riesling and craft beer.

Brittany Pansino
Operations Assistant
Brittany Pansino brings a wealth of administrative and wine experience to Michael Corso Selections. Prior to joining the company, she spent nearly a decade in the building materials industry, and brings with her supply chain, data management, and fast-paced customer service experience to the team. She has been making wine with her husband’s family for over 13 years (though, the in-laws have been doing it for far longer!), using traditional old-world Italian equipment. She holds a WSET L2 in wines, and has a passion for French wines, but has yet to meet a wine she doesn’t like, and can’t pass up the opportunity to try something she’s never heard of. Brittany has a BA in History from DePaul University, and enjoys travel, live music, cooking, and taking full advantage of Chicago’s robust restaurant scene, especially during patio season.

results.rawContent:
Welcome to De Maison Selections
A Curated World of Wine, Spirits, and Ciders
Wines of integrity, stories with soul
De Maison Selections is the exclusive US importer of exceptional, artisanal properties from Spain, France, Japan, and beyond, which are rooted in their land and demonstrate respect for their ecology and heritage. As a result, our releases are imbued with a unique cultural stamp and authenticity.
It is this originality of identity and commitment to sustainability which drives the next generation of independent artisans. Innovation and bettering the status quo are at the core of our philosophy.
“Del most flor, amb la dedicació i el rigor de l’obra artesanal ben feta.”
This Catalan saying that graces the label of the first wine we imported, Avinyó Cava, translates to:“Starting with the best part of the harvest, and exerting the dedication and rigor of a well-crafted work.”  
It has guided the direction of our company since 1996. We believe that respecting the integrity of the source material with care and intention leads to deeper cultural connection, better wine, and lasting relationships.
Introducing the Porróncast: Voices from Vine to Glass
The Porróncast is our podcast series that brings you the stories of winemakers, distillers, restaurateurs, and creatives who share the Porrón, and what drives their passion for their craft. Hosted by Ryan Looper, with frequent appearances by other members of the De Maison team, each episode brings you inside the minds shaping the future of our industry.
Live from Pass the Porrón: The Gold Coast of Rioja & Reclaiming Place with André Tamers
October 9, 2026
This panel discussion was recorded live during
Pass the Porrón, De Maison’s 30th birthday celebration, on Friday, April 24th 2026.Can a famous wine region reinvent itself without losing its audience?
In this live panel discussion led by De Maison Selections founder André Tamers, we explore the changing landscape of Rioja as it transitions from traditional brand-driven consistency toward site-specificity, terroir, and wines of place. Joined by four independent grower-producers from the De Maison portfolio, André tackles one of the biggest questions in the wine world today: When a region’s commercial success is built on a uniform, recognizable identity, how do you reframe the narrative around quality and origin without leaving consumers behind?
The panel goes deep on why Rioja is often misunderstood, and why place and village identity is the clearest path forward, engaging with topics like: time versus place, how labeling rules shape what you see on a bottle, and what has to change for small producers to survive and thrive.
In this episode, the panel covers:
Terroir vs. Aging: How traditional aging classifications can flatten diversity, and why Reserva and Gran Reserva can coexist with village wines when terroir leads the story.
Village Microclimates: How limestone soils drive acidity in Samaniego whites, altitude brings freshness to Labastida, and river-influenced terraces shape San Vicente.
Rethinking Oak: The role of oak as a complementary tool rather than the dominant flavor profile.
Industry Action: What importers, retailers, and educators must do as Rioja portfolios become more granular and place-focused.
Guest Panel:
Pablo Rodríguez of Remelluri
Alain Quintana representing the Cosecheros de Labastida
Maríasun Saenz de Samaniego from Ostatu
Carlos Yécora of Luberri
Listen on:
